message.content:
I'm doing a responsive (mobile/tablet/desktop) audit of the FlowGuard client at C:\Users\felth\Downloads\FlowGuard\client.

For EACH of these pages and its associated CSS file(s), read the JSX and CSS and report concrete responsiveness problems. Be specific: cite file path + line numbers + the exact offending CSS/JSX.

Pages (src/pages unless noted): Dashboard.jsx, Cameras.jsx, CameraInventory.jsx, ObjectDetection.jsx, DetectionSettings.jsx, VPatrol.jsx, GateScanner.jsx, Attendance.jsx, TenantLogistics.jsx, DriverPass.jsx, Users.jsx, SecurityReview.jsx, IncidentDashboard.jsx, SupportDashboard.jsx, TenantManagement.jsx, Settings.jsx, Login.jsx, Register.jsx. Also src/components/Sidebar.jsx.

Associated CSS is in src/css/ (e.g. Dashboard.css, Cameras.css, ObjectDetection.css, VPatrol.css, Users.css, Management.css, IncidentDashboard.css, SupportDashboard.css, Settings.css, Login.css, Attendance.css, Booking.css, DriverPass.css, CameraFeed.css, Global.css, App.css). Map each page to the CSS it imports.

Specifically hunt for and list, per file:
- fixed px widths that would overflow a 390px phone (width: NNNpx, min-width large values)
- large min-width on tables/containers
- tables that will clip / have no horizontal scroll wrapper
- action buttons that could extend outside cards
- font sizes that get too small on mobile
- forms/grids that stay multi-column on phones (grid-template-columns with fixed multi-col, no media query)
- modals wider/taller than viewport (no max-width/max-height/overflow)
- camera/video/img containers without max-width:100% or object-fit
- any existing @media breakpoints already present (list the breakpoint px values used across the codebase so I can stay consistent)
- hover-only interactions
- touch targets clearly < 44px

Also report: which pages render data in <table> elements (candidates for table→card on mobile), and which use a shared layout wrapper class (e.g. a `.page`, `.dashboard-container`, `.main-content` etc.).

Give me a structured per-file list plus a summary of the existing breakpoint values already used in the codebase. Do NOT edit anything — read only.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
I have enough to compile a thorough audit. Here are the concrete, per-file responsiveness findings.

## Shared architecture (applies to most pages)

- **Layout wrapper**: Every authenticated page uses `<div className="dashboard-layout">` + `<Sidebar/>` + `<main className="dashboard-main …">`. `.dashboard-layout` (`src/css/Dashboard.css:4`) is `display:flex; height:100vh; overflow:hidden`. The sidebar is `width:240px; min-width:240px` (`Dashboard.css:33-35`) and collapses to an off-canvas drawer with a hamburger at `@media (max-width:768px)` (`Dashboard.css:786-873`). `.dashboard-main` gets `padding:90px 20px 20px` on mobile (`Dashboard.css:851`) so content clears the fixed hamburger.
- **Auth pages** (Login, Register, ForgotKey, ResetPassword) use `.login-container`/`.login-box` instead, no sidebar.

### Existing breakpoints in the codebase (inconsistent — this is the big one)
- `480px`: AIChatPopup, Enrollment, Home, IncidentDashboard, SupportDashboard
- `600px`: Home, IncidentDashboard (`inc-form-grid`)
- `640px`: VPatrol
- `760px`: **Cameras, ObjectDetection** (note: NOT 768)
- `768px`: Dashboard (sidebar/hamburger), Management, Users, Settings, Attendance, Booking, SupportDashboard, IncidentDashboard, Footer, NavBar, Home; `min-width:768` in DriverPass
- `850px`: Contact
- `900px`: AIInnovation, FacialEvaluation
- `1024px`: Dashboard, Booking, IncidentDashboard, SupportDashboard, VPatrol
- `1099px`: Home
- `1180px`: Cameras, ObjectDetection
- `1366px` (+ `min-width:769`): Users

The sidebar/hamburger switch happens at **768px**, but Cameras/ObjectDetection collapse their own grids at **760px** and VPatrol at **640px** — so there are 8px / 128px windows where the sidebar is already a drawer but the page grid hasn't reflowed yet (or vice-versa). Recommend standardizing on 768 / 1024 / 480.

### Pages that render `<table>` (table→card candidates)
IncidentDashboard, SupportDashboard, SecurityReview, TenantLogistics, Users, TenantManagement, Attendance (plus out-of-scope FacialEvaluation, StaffManagement, UserLogs). Management.css does a global table→card conversion at `@media(max-width:768px)` (`src/css/Management.css:439-501`) driven by `td::before { content: attr(data-label) }` (`Management.css:475`).

---

## Per-file findings

### Sidebar.jsx + Dashboard.css (shared)
- `src/components/Sidebar.jsx:94-135` nav links → `.sidebar-nav a { padding:12px 20px; font-size:0.9rem }` (`Dashboard.css:83-88`) ≈ 40px tall — **just under the 44px touch target**.
- Sidebar is purely hover-driven for active state on desktop (`Dashboard.css:93-98`) — fine (also uses `.active`), no action needed.
- Off-canvas drawer/hamburger logic is solid; hamburger is 45px (`Dashboard.css:794-795`), good.

### Dashboard.jsx → Dashboard.css
- Generally well-handled: grids collapse at 1024 then 768 (`Dashboard.css:779-784`).
- `.charts-section` desktop `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(320px, 420px))` (`Dashboard.css:585`) — the fixed **320px min** would overflow a 390px column if it weren't overridden; it *is* reset to `1fr` at ≤1024 (`Dashboard.css:783`), so OK, but the 320px min is fragile.
- No `@media` below 768; on a 390px phone everything is `1fr`, acceptable.

### Cameras.jsx → Dashboard.css + Cameras.css
- `.camera-metrics { grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(150px, 1fr)) }` (`Cameras.css:130`) needs ~600px; only collapses at **760px** (`Cameras.css:858-864`). In the **769–1180px** tablet range the sidebar is back (240px) and 4×150px overflows the shrunken content area.
- `.cameras-main .camera-grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(280px, 1fr)) }` (`Cameras.css:206`) = 560px min; same tablet overflow risk before the 760 breakpoint.
- `.camera-console { grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) 360px }` (`Cameras.css:174`) — fixed 360px 2nd column; collapses at 1180 (OK).
- `.camera-row-actions button { width:30px; height:30px }` (`Cameras.css:597-600`) and `.camera-icon-btn { width:38px }` (`Cameras.css:121`) — **below 44px touch target**.
- Camera video is fine: `.camera-feed-placeholder` `aspect-ratio:4/3` + `.camera-video { object-fit:contain; width/height:100% }` (`Dashboard.css:792-811`).

### CameraInventory.jsx → Dashboard.css + Cameras.css
- `.camera-admin-layout { grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) 340px }` (`Cameras.css:427-429`) fixed 340px column, collapses at 1180 (OK).
- `.camera-inventory-summary { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(160px,1fr)) }` (`Cameras.css:447-449`) = 480px min; collapses at 760 — tablet overflow window (769–1180) with sidebar present.
- Same 30px action buttons (`Cameras.css:597`) — sub-44px touch targets.
- Renders camera rows (not a `<table>`), so no clipping issue.

### ObjectDetection.jsx → Dashboard.css + ObjectDetection.css
- Video handled well: `.od-video-stage { width:100%; aspect-ratio:16/9; overflow:hidden }` + `.od-stream-img { object-fit:cover }` (`ObjectDetection.css:360-395`), hardware variant `aspect-ratio:4/3` + `object-fit:contain` (`:397-408`).
- Grids collapse at 1180 then 760 (`ObjectDetection.css:1292-1324`).
- `.od-command-strip / .od-grid` use fixed 2nd tracks e.g. `minmax(360px, 0.7fr)` (`:248`) and `repeat(4, minmax(160px,1fr))` (`:195`) — 640px+ min; only reflow at 1180, so 769–1180 tablet can overflow before collapse. Font sizes drop to `0.66rem`/`0.68rem` (`:1231, :1041`) which is very small on mobile.

### DetectionSettings.jsx → Dashboard.css + ObjectDetection.css
- Shares ObjectDetection grids (`.od-settings-grid`, `.od-rule-form`, `.od-zone-summary-grid`) which collapse at 1180/760 (`ObjectDetection.css:1295, 1318`). Same tablet-window overflow and tiny fonts as above.

### VPatrol.jsx → Dashboard.css + VPatrol.css
- **Hamburger overlap bug**: `.vpatrol-main { padding:30px }` (`VPatrol.css:34-39`) has no equal specificity but is imported *after* Dashboard.css, so it overrides `.dashboard-main`'s mobile `padding:90px 20px 20px`. At ≤768 the fixed hamburger (top 15px, 45px tall) **overlaps the VPatrol header** because padding-top stays 30px. The ≤1024 block only adds `overflow-y:auto` (`VPatrol.css:513`), it never restores top padding.
- `.vpatrol-grid { grid-template-columns: 1.5fr 1fr }` (`VPatrol.css:4-8`) collapses to column at 1024 (`:508, :514`) — OK.
- `.vpatrol-card { height:480px }` fixed (`:15`) reset to `auto` at 1024 (`:509`) — OK.
- Video fine: `.cctv-container { width:100%; overflow:hidden }` + `.video-feed { object-fit:contain }` (`VPatrol.css:165-185`).
- Small controls: `.item-action-btn` font `0.65rem` (`:479`), `.timeline-clear-btn` padding 6px (`:448`) — small tap targets/fonts.

### GateScanner.jsx → Dashboard.css + VPatrol.css
- **Same hamburger overlap bug**: `.gate-main { padding:30px }` (`VPatrol.css:82-87`) overrides `.dashboard-main` mobile padding; ≤1024 only adds `overflow-y:auto` (`:527`). Header sits under the hamburger on phones.
- `.gate-status-card { min-width:280px }` (`VPatrol.css:112`) — fine on 390px, becomes full width at ≤1024 (`:537-543`).
- `GateScanner.jsx:648` inline `style={{ width:'100%', height:'100%' }}` on `.cctv-container` — fine.
- Video/canvas handled via `.video-feed` (object-fit contain) — OK.

### Attendance.jsx → Dashboard.css + Management.css + Attendance.css
- **Table has NO `data-label` attributes** (confirmed: 0 occurrences in Attendance.jsx) but uses `<table className="management-table">` (`Attendance.jsx:139`). At ≤768 the global card conversion (`Management.css:439-482`) hides `<thead>` and relies on `td::before{content:attr(data-label)}` — so **mobile cards show values with no field labels**. Attendance.css:183-199 also `!important`-forces every td to `display:flex; justify-content:flex-start` and strips right-margins, compounding the label loss.
- `.attendance-metrics-grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(3,1fr) }` (`Attendance.css:70`) collapses to 1fr at 768 (`:152`) — OK.
- Note conflicting intent: Attendance.css:168-173 sets `.table-container{overflow-x:auto}` at ≤768 while Management.css converts the same table to full-width cards — the horizontal scroll never triggers, harmless but dead.

### TenantLogistics.jsx → Dashboard.css + Management.css + Booking.css
- Well-handled. Bookings table `.active-bookings .management-table { min-width:820px }` (`Booking.css:196`) with wrapper `overflow-x:auto` (`:195`), and min-width dropped to 0 at ≤768 (`:251`) where it becomes cards (has `data-label`, 8 occurrences). 
- Modal `.booking-modal { max-width:520px; max-height:88vh; overflow-y:auto }` (`Booking.css:359-365`) — good.
- `.logistics-stats { repeat(4,1fr) }` → 2 at 1024 → 1 at 768 (`Booking.css:288-290, 391-395`) — OK.
- `.logistics-search { min-width:220px }` (`Booking.css:311`) fits 390px.

### DriverPass.jsx → DriverPass.css (+ Login.css via import chain not used here)
- Mobile-first and clean: `.pass-card { width: min(100% - 24px, 420px) }` (`DriverPass.css:18`), QR `width: min(230px, 64vw)` (`:81`). No issues. Desktop centering at `min-width:768` (`:167`).

### Users.jsx → Dashboard.css + Users.css
- Well-handled. `.table-wrapper { overflow-x:auto }` (`Users.css:166-174`), table→card at 768 (`:478-515`, uses `data-label`, 7 occurrences), modal `.security-modal { width:100%; max-width:450px }` (`:545-555`).
- `.user-summary-grid { repeat(4, minmax(140px,1fr)) }` (`:5-7`) = 560px min; `.user-filter-bar { minmax(220px,2fr) repeat(3,minmax(140px,1fr)) }` (`:35-37`) = 640px min — both only collapse at 768 (`:479-482`), so **769–1366px** tablet can overflow (partly mitigated by the 1366 tightening block `:651`).
- `.presence-tag`/action width `118px` (`Users.css:366`) fine.

### SecurityReview.jsx → Dashboard.css + Management.css
- Best-handled table: `.review-table-container { overflow-x:auto }` (`Management.css:537`), `.security-review-table { min-width:900px }` (`:539`) explicitly reset to `min-width:0` at ≤768 (`:569-578`) with cells stacking. Has `data-label` (6). No issue.

### IncidentDashboard.jsx → Dashboard.css + Management.css + Users.css + IncidentDashboard.css
- **Table conflict + missing labels**: `<table className="management-table inc-table">` (`IncidentDashboard.jsx:494`). `.management-table.inc-table { min-width:880px; table-layout:fixed }` (`IncidentDashboard.css:715-718`) is **never reset at any mobile breakpoint**, yet the global Management card conversion (`Management.css:439`) still fires at ≤768 (it matches `.management-table`). Result on phone: `<thead>` hidden, `td`s become blocks, **but the table keeps `min-width:880px`** so it renders 880px wide and horizontally scrolls inside `.inc-table-wrap` — a half-converted card/table hybrid. Also IncidentDashboard.jsx has **no `data-label`** attributes, so if the card layout wins the labels are blank.
- **Detail modal has no height cap**: `.inc-detail-modal { width:90%; max-width:620px }` (`IncidentDashboard.css:232-241`) — **no `max-height`/`overflow`**, unlike the create modal which has `max-height:90vh; overflow-y:auto` (`:435-436`). A long incident detail can exceed an 812px phone viewport and clip.
- Stat grid reflows well: 4→2 (1024) →`1fr 1fr` (768) →1 (480) (`:335-371`).
- Sticky actions column (`:749-762`) relies on `position:sticky; right:0` — meaningless once the table becomes blocks on mobile.

### SupportDashboard.jsx → Dashboard.css + Management.css + SupportDashboard.css
- Transcript modal is good: `.support-transcript-modal { max-width:560px; width:92%; max-height:80vh; overflow:hidden }` with inner `overflow-y:auto` (`SupportDashboard.css:210-228`).
- Tables use `.management-table` with `data-label` (12) → card conversion works.
- `.sup-stats-grid { repeat(4,1fr) }` → 2 (1024) → 1 (480) (`:23-79`) — note it jumps 4→2 at 1024 and stays 2-col down to 481px; 2 columns at ~390px would be cramped but it's only ≤480 that goes single — fine since 480<390? No, 390<480 so single-column applies. OK.
- `SupportDashboard.jsx:330` inline `style={{ width:'160px' … }}` on a select inside a table cell — fixed 160px; fits inside the mobile card, but hard-coded.

### TenantManagement.jsx → Management.css
- Uses `.management-container` + `<table className="management-table">` with `data-label` (3). Card conversion works at 768. Modal `.modal-content { max-width:450px; width:90% }` →95% at 768 (`Management.css:299-308, 503-506`). 
- Note: imports **only** Management.css (not Dashboard.css) — but it still renders `.dashboard-layout`/`.dashboard-main` (`TenantManagement.jsx:103-105`). Those classes live in Dashboard.css, which isn't imported here. It works only because Dashboard.css is globally bundled via other pages; **in isolation the layout/sidebar would be unstyled**. Worth flagging as a fragile dependency.

### Settings.jsx → Dashboard.css + Settings.css
- Well-handled: `.setting-row` goes column at 768, `.dark-select` becomes full width (`Settings.css:121-140`). `.setting-control { min-width:200px }` (`:63`) fits 390px. No issues.

### Login.jsx / Register.jsx → Login.css (Login also imports DriverPass.css)
- **Login.css has zero `@media` queries.** Layout survives via `.login-container { width:100%; max-width:420px }` (`Login.css:20-24`) and `.login-box { padding:40px }` (`:45`). On a 360–390px phone the 40px card padding + `.login-content-area` 20px side padding (`:16`) is heavy but doesn't overflow (`box-sizing:border-box` on inputs, `:84`). Consider reducing card padding under ~400px.
- Register is a single-column `.input-group` stack, all `width:100%` (`Register.jsx:83-146`); the role `<select>` uses inline `width:100%` (`:125`) — fine. No multi-column form to worry about.

---

## Highest-impact fixes to prioritize
1. **VPatrol & GateScanner hamburger overlap** — `.vpatrol-main`/`.gate-main` `padding:30px` (`VPatrol.css:34, 82`) defeats the mobile `padding-top:90px`; header hides under the hamburger.
2. **IncidentDashboard `.inc-table` min-width:880px never reset** (`IncidentDashboard.css:715`) → broken hybrid table on phones; and add `data-label`s or opt it out of the Management card rules.
3. **IncidentDashboard detail modal missing `max-height`/`overflow`** (`IncidentDashboard.css:232-241`).
4. **Attendance & IncidentDashboard tables lack `data-label`** → unlabeled mobile cards.
5. **760px vs 768px breakpoint mismatch** (Cameras/ObjectDetection) creates tablet overflow windows for the 4-col `.camera-metrics` / `.od` grids.
6. **Sub-44px touch targets**: `.camera-row-actions button` 30px (`Cameras.css:597`), `.camera-icon-btn` 38px (`:121`), sidebar links ~40px, VPatrol `.item-action-btn`/`.timeline-clear-btn`.

No files were modified.
